### FIXED LUNA <note>SILVER</note>.

Let Luna <note>silver</note> be cemented for six days in <term>crocus of Mars</term> <note>iron oxide</note>. Let it not be further affected by <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note>, and it will take the tincture.

### FIXATION OF MERCURY OUT OF R.

->Take Mercury, 6 parts.<-
->Borax, 4 ounces.<-

Mix them into a paste properly together until the Mercury is completely invisible. Pound and <term>sublime</term> <note>vaporize and condense</note> until the rising stops, repeating the process until this takes place; then cool. Break the subliming vessel. <term>Fulminate</term> <note>refine in a furnace</note> that which is found at the bottom of it. You will then have the best Luna <note>silver</note>; also, in the first eight ounces of this Luna, you will have 2½ ounces of the best Sol <note>gold</note>.

### NOTE OF MASTER ALBERTUS.

Prepare salt by frequent dissolution in fire, melting and congealing. Repeat this until it melts like wax, fifteen times employing a filter, etc. Also, afterwards take 4 parts of borax, and pound it with well-calcined alum. Pound it again, even seven times. Then take the said salt and white borax in equal quantities. Put it in a glass vessel moderately warm. Then a tincture is produced from this. One part of it is projected over 30 parts of Mercury, and the same becomes Luna <note>silver</note>, commencing to flow immediately with the tincture. Blow strongly so that the Mercury may make its way through. Melt it, and you will have Luna. *Notice carefully.*

### FIXATION OF LUNA <note>SILVER</note>.

Dissolve eight ounces of Luna <note>silver</note> in <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note>. Afterwards, let it congeal. Add to this <term>calx</term> <note>powdered residue</note> the same quantity of sublimated Mercury. <term>Sublime</term> <note>vaporize and condense</note> 15 times, as frequently soaking and drying, until all that is there is absorbed. Afterwards, reduce the dross into a body with <term>oil of tartar</term> <note>potassium carbonate solution</note>, and you will have Luna to the weight of the gold, and it stands in cement.

### NOTE FOR LUNA <note>SILVER</note>.

Take a globule of earth and fill it with Mercury. Put it into Saturn <note>lead</note> for three or four hours. Afterwards, Saturn attracts Mercury to itself. Over this Saturn and Mercury, project fixed borax with saltpeter into the <term>tigillum</term> <note>crucible</note>. Next, <term>fulminate</term> <note>refine</note> in a wind furnace. This will test the Luna.

### WATER OF MERCURY.

Take equal parts of tartar and mercury, <term>sublime</term> <note>vaporize and condense</note> three times, and pound on marble. Then dissolve it. The metal is dissolved in that water in one hour, but the matter is to be distilled in water. Afterwards, take equal parts of pure gold and pure Luna <note>silver</note>. Dissolve them in the aforesaid water. Then take one part each of borax and camphor. <term>Reverberate</term> <note>heat in a reflecting furnace</note> one-half of these, distill the water from them and keep it. Next, take one drop of this water and project it into the water in which the body has been dissolved. Place it on a slow fire for seven days, and it will become milk. Replace this, and make in turn two or three drops. Repeat this process until it no longer grows white, but another red liquid remains. Coagulate this; then take one part of the white powder and

### SECRET NOTE.

Take filings of copper <note>Venus</note> and put them in wax for three days and nights. Take one pound of that, four pounds of vitriol, and five of sulfur. Mix them; seal <note>lute</note> between two bricks in a carefully watched furnace, and note the result.

### IN THE DISTILLATION OF VITRIOL FOR FIXATION.

Place camphor in a glass vessel containing oil, and it will become fixed.

### NOTE ON PARS CUM PARTE.

Pour <term>pars cum parte</term> <note>an alloy of equal parts gold and silver</note> several times into blessed oil. It gains in grade and acquires great softness.

### RUBIFICATION <note>REDDENING</note>.

Take vitriol and pound it small on marble. Saturate <note>imbibe</note> it with wine to the consistency of a paste. Then take two stone dishes, one somewhat larger than the other. Place the saturated vitriol inside, and seal <note>lute</note> with a material composed of dung and gravel. Put it in a furnace for the space of a natural day <note>24 hours</note>, and the thing is done.

### THE PURIFICATION OF TIN.

Project three or four times over oil of tartar.

### NOTE.

Oil of tartar is that which is made for common use; but if a plate of copper be frequently placed in it, it becomes white.

### FOR BROKEN COINS.

Take sal ammoniac, place it in the crack, and the damage <note>lesion</note> disappears over a coal fire.

### SAL AMMONIAC IS MADE THUS.

Take twenty parts of urine passed by a wine-drinker. Skim it and let it cool. Add one pound of sublimated dung and two pounds of salt. Mix these and let it stand for three days; then boil until it solidifies <note>coagulated</note>.

### FOR REDDENING CRYSTAL.

Take olive oil and quicklime in any quantity, and shake them well together. Then take two parts of salt alkali and one part of common salt. Mix these so that the oil shall float on the top to the depth of one finger. Distill over a slow fire and let it cool. Set a light to it, and, if it burns, the process is not complete. Repeat until it no longer kindles, and then it is made ready for reddening <note>rubifying</note> the crystal.

### FIXATION OF MERCURY.

Sublimate with quicklime until complete.

### FOR GILDING.

Distill the yolk of eggs. It is converted into a red oil which gilds money and lasts forever.

### SAL AMMONIAC.

Take one pound of <term>sal ammoniac</term>, pour <term>acetum</term> and wine over it, distill it using a filter, and add ten pounds of sublimated dung. Set it to boil until it is dried out. Pour urine on it again until one-twentieth part of it is consumed. Then add pure water and dissolve it. Take the clear water and set aside the dregs. Boil and dry it, either in the sun or in the shade.

### SAL BORAX.

Take <term>calcined tartar</term>. Pour warm water over it. Pass this through a straining-bag until the upper part is clear. Then take <term>common salt</term> dissolved in water, add one part of this, and afterward boil it in an iron dish until it thickens. Then place it in a vessel and dry it until it becomes crumbly. In this way, you will have <term>borax</term>, which you should place in a glass vessel.

### ANOTHER METHOD.

Take one-third part of <term>crude tartar</term>. Sift it thoroughly and add six parts of prepared <term>common salt</term>. Boil it for a day until it is converted into liquid. Set it to cool and distill it using a filter; afterward, let it boil until it hardens, and you will have the very best <term>borax</term>.

### SAL BORAX FOR GOLDSMITHS.

Take one part each of starch, <term>mastic</term>, and <term>sulphur</term>. From this mixture take two parts, pulverize them, and boil until thickened. Set it in a glass vessel to putrefy for four weeks, and you will have <term>borax</term>.

### SAL BORAX.

->Take<-

| Ingredient | Quantity |
| :--- | :--- |
| <term>Calcined Tartar</term> | 1/2 lb. |
| <term>Quick Lime</term> | 2 lb. |
| <term>Wood Ashes</term> | 1 lb. |
| <term>Crude Tartar</term> | 1 1/2 lb. |
| Prepared <term>Common Salt</term> | 6 lb. |

Boil all of these together, distill through a filter, and coagulate. In this way, excellent <term>borax</term> is obtained.

### LAZURIUM.

Take one part of <term>sal ammoniac</term>, two parts of <term>sulphur</term>, and two parts of <term>mercury</term>. Mix them and proceed as directed above for <term>cinnabar</term> until a purple smoke rises; then stop.

### ANOTHER AND BETTER METHOD.

Take <term>lapis lazuli</term>. Heat and crush it. Then take two and a half parts of <term>pitch</term>, <term>goat suet</term>, and <term>oil of laurel</term>. Dissolve these together.

### ANOTHER METHOD.

Take <term>sal ammoniac</term> and pulverize it. Amalgamate this with four parts of <term>mercury</term>, and place it in a glass vessel that is tightly sealed <note>luted</note>. Sublimate it for one hour. Then gradually increase the heat until it reaches the smoke of <term>citron wood</term>; afterward, decrease the heat. Finally, you will find <term>lazurium</term> at the bottom.

### ANOTHER.

Take <term>sulphur</term> and <term>mercury</term>. Amalgamate them as described above and sublimate.

### FLOS AERIS.

Take filings of Venus <note>copper</note>, urine, and sal ammoniac. Mix them together, dry them, and soak them a second time.

### CINNABRIUM.

Take sulfur; dissolve one part of it and two parts of mercury. Cool them, place them in a glazed vessel, and sublimate. First, a purple smoke ascends, and afterward a red one. Then stop.

### TO MAKE MARBLE.

Take quicklime and extract the lye <note>lixivium</note> with wine. Soak calcined and pounded flint with this. It immediately becomes capable of taking color.

### CORALS ARE MADE THUS :

Take one part of minium <note>red lead</note> and half a part of cinnabar, but five parts each of quicklime and lime of flint, with a sufficient quantity of the above-mentioned lye <note>lixivium</note> and the white of eggs. Add as much salt as you like, and finally boil in linseed oil.

### FACTITIOUS CORALS.

Take two parts of good gypsum, half a part of pure lime, and half a part each of minium and cinnabar, with a sufficient quantity of egg white. Shape and dry.

### PEARLS FROM CHALK.

Put chalk in the fire until it is crumbly. Mix with the white of eggs and shape. Then harden, and afterward moisten with saliva. Whiten with silver tablets and harden again with fine powder, either in the sun or over a coal fire, as you please.

### TO MAKE PEARLS BETTER THAN NATURAL ONES.

Take mother of pearl and pulverize it very finely, afterward adding fine flour. Mix and blend this with May-dew. Shape as you wish. Then give them to hungry pigeons to eat. Wash their dung, and you will find very fine pearls. But note that the pigeons should be kept for three days without anything to eat.

### ANOTHER MODE.

Take mother of pearl, boil it, and wash it well. Then take the same quantity of crystal, pound it small, and mix with the white of eggs. Shape and dry. Afterward, boil thoroughly in linseed oil, and wash with white wine. Afterward, dry in the sun or over a fire.

### NOTE FOR LUNA.

Take one part each of arsenic and of sublimated mercury, and sublimate them by themselves. Add an equal weight of quicklime. Soak with water of fixed sal ammoniac, then cover with wax and place on the fire. Sublimate three times, and keep in a closed vessel. Afterward, dry it and project <note>add to molten metal</note> one part over twenty-five parts of purified Venus <note>copper</note>. Thus Luna <note>silver</note> will be produced.

### RUBY.

Take 4 lbs. of the strongest vinegar <note>acetum</note>, not distilled, and in it put one <term>🜪</term> <note>ounce</note> of atramentum <note>vitriol or black pigment</note>. Distill this in the manner of aquafortis <note>nitric acid</note>, and at last with a

->AQUA ARDENS: OR WATER OF MERCURY.<-

Take half a pound of sal ammoniac, a sufficient quantity of tartar and live sulfur, with one pound of common salt, and a quart of good white wine. Place all these in a well-luted <note>sealed</note> vessel and subject it to the fire, perhaps somewhat severely. Then keep the water well away from the wind. This purifies metals and converts mercury into pure Luna <note>silver</note>.

->WATER OF SULPHUR.<-

Take 1/2 lb. of sulfur and 4 1/2 lb. of saltpeter. Place these in a well-luted <note>sealed</note> vessel, and put it in the ashes for twenty-four hours. Remove and pulverize. Then mix one-fourth of this with 3 oz. of pure water; whereupon the water is turned to a red color, and money can be colored with it into the appearance of most beautiful Sol <note>gold</note>.

->AURUM MUSICUM.<-

Take of tin and of sulfur each one-third part, amalgamate, and pulverize. Afterward wash, first with lixivium <note>lye</note> and then with pure water, until no dirt comes off. Then dry. Next take two pounds of Mercurius vivus <note>quicksilver/mercury</note> and the same quantity of sal ammoniac. Mortify the mercury with acetum <note>vinegar</note>, and at the same time wash it, as before. Then place it in a well-luted <note>sealed</note> vial, so that the glass vessel is half full. Heat it in sand for four hours until you see a golden smoke ascend.

->WONDERS OF ANTIMONY.<-

Take antimony and purify it with calcined tartar. Afterward make aqua fortis. Dissolve it in the water, and congeal it, either in the aqua fortis or by itself. Then it will be an oil incapable of mixture—oil or stone—in the proportion of one part on three parts of Saturn <note>lead</note>; and it will be silver answering perfectly to every test.

->WONDERFUL AQUA ARDENS.<-

Take old red wine; and put in a glazed vessel one part of orpiment <note>auripigment</note>, half of quick sulfur, and a fourth of quicklime. Mix together; afterward distill by means of a rose alembic and the thing is done.

### THE VIRTUES OF THIS WATER.

Whoever places his finger in it is burned as if by a flame. In like manner, a rag placed in it burns like a candle and is not extinguished by water.

### AUGMENTATION.

Make an amalgam of mercury and Luna <note>silver</note>. Then fill a vessel with quicklime. Take equal parts of alkali salt and of litharge. Put layer upon layer and let it stand for a day and a night. Afterward, let it dissolve.

### ON RED VENUS.

Take equal parts of crushed beans and of crude tartar, together with a quantity of tutia <note>zinc oxide</note> exceeding one of those parts. Mix all well together and place layer upon layer with plates of Venus <note>copper</note> which have been laid all night in acetum <note>vinegar</note>. Pour it over the layer, and let it take shape wherever it can be poured. You will see the result.

### CALCINATION OF JOVE AND SATURN TO WHITE.

Make layer upon layer with quicklime and the above-mentioned metals <note>tin and lead</note>. Cement by night, then take it again, dissolve, and pour into a lixivium <note>alkaline solution</note> of quicklime, acetum <note>vinegar</note>, and vine-ashes. It will then be as Luna <note>silver</note>.

### TO REDUCE CALCINED BODIES TO THEIR ORIGINAL MATTER.

Take one-fifth of the metal and two pounds of borax of tartar. Pour them together and place them in an iron vessel. It will be as Luna <note>silver</note>, and can easily become Sol <note>gold</note> and Luna <note>silver</note> if first saturated with oil of tartar.

### CALCINATION OF SOL AND LUNA.

Take filings of Sol <note>gold</note> and place them in acetum <note>vinegar</note> for nine days. Then put them in water of sal ammoniac. Saturate them well; then dry them, and continue the process as long as you please.

### THE DEVIL IN ALCHEMY.

Dissolve, fix, coagulate, and repeat.

### WATER OF ALKALI SALT.

Take alkali, sal ammoniac, and eggshells. Pound them together with good acetum <note>vinegar</note>, and dissolve them at the same time.

### PURIFICATION OF SULFUR.

Take pounded sulfur, pour acetum <note>vinegar</note> and wine on it, let it boil for a day, and skim it. Then pour in urine and boil for two hours. Do this until it ceases to froth. Whatever body there is does not float in the urine, but the urine is clear and sufficient for the purpose.

### THE SUBLIMATION AND FIXATION OF SULFUR, SO THAT IT BECOMES WHITE.

Take as much sulfur as you will and pound it. Pour acetum <note>vinegar</note> upon it. Heat it until all fatness <note>oily impurities</note> is removed, and then lay it aside. Secondly, heat it as before in boys’ urine, and draw off the fatness. Next, pound it with prepared alum, place it in a sublimatory <note>a vessel for sublimation</note> and sublimate for three hours. Then the white sulfur ascends like snow and flows down upon the coals just like a snowstorm.

### OIL OF VITRIOL.

Take as much vitriol as you wish and distill it by descent. It produces a bright green oil, and is called milk of mercury. However, it must be heated over a large fire; it is similar in its nature to balsam.

### ANOTHER METHOD.

Distill vitriol with an alembic over a very strong fire for three days and nights. Let it be soaked <note>imbibed</note> three times with its dregs, and then distilled from them. Afterward, distill it five or six times, and thus a great arcanum is produced.

### CORRECTION OF THIS PROCESS.

After the third distillation, mix it with a half portion of burning wine <note>vinum ardens</note> and distill as mentioned before.

### ANOTHER VERY EXPEDITIOUS MODE.

Take vitriol and distill it vigorously by descent, then by an alembic, and then by a water bath <note>balneum Mariæ</note>. Finally, do this twice or thrice by means of a retort; the method is subtle. Some say they have seen the oil of vitriol distilled until a whiteness like milk appeared.

### PREPARATION OF COMMON SALT.

Create layer upon layer with quicklime. Let it be cemented well, distill through a filter, and coagulate.

### ANOTHER.

Take urine, quicklime, and salt; reduce it to water and boil. Then put them in a vessel, add <note>project</note> it to water, and coagulate. Place it in the vessel again and repeat the process; it is ignited at length, whether that is sufficient or not.

### FUSION OF A MARCASITE.

Take three-tenths of the marcasite, 1/2 [part] of Saturn <note>lead</note>, 3 ounces <note>iij. ℥</note> of Venus <note>copper</note>, and 4 pounds <note>iiiij. ℔</note> of iron dross <note>scoria of iron</note>. At the same time, it is poured upon 4 [parts] of Luna <note>silver</note>, a square <note>□</note> of Saturn <note>lead</note>, and a pound <note>℔</note> of Venus <note>copper</note>.

### ALKALI IS MADE THUS:

Take wood ashes, quicklime, and the ash of beans. Extract the lye <note>lixivium</note> and coagulate.

### THE SUBLIMATION OF SAL AMMONIAC.

Take equal parts of the salt itself and of pulverized Mars <note>iron</note>, and sublimate.

### CROCUS OF MARS.

Take nitric acid <note>aquafortis</note>, not too strong. Place it on filings of Mars <note>iron</note> and let it stand for several days. Then heat it over a coal fire until it becomes red.

### ANOTHER METHOD.

Take antimony, filings of Mars <note>iron</note>, and crude tartar. Dissolve them together, and a good crocus <note>powder</note> is produced.

### SAL BORAX OF THE PHILOSOPHERS IN WHICH ALL METALS AND GLASS ARE FUSED.

Take bull's milk <note>lac tauri</note> purified by a filter, alkali, borax, rock salt <note>gem-salt</note>, and goat's blood in equal parts. Mix with water, put in a vial, and dry <note>desiccate</note>. Then Venus <note>copper</note> or any other substance, whether metal or glass, is fused within it.

### SALTPETRE.

Take quicklime and warm water. Stir for six days and distill by means of a filter. Place it in the Sun <note>☉</note> until it is consumed, and you will have saltpetre.

## THE SOLUTION OF SOL FROM SILVER.

Take one part of calcined tartar with two parts of sal ammoniac. Place them on marble and then in a glass vessel. Then take the root of pellitory, pound it with acetum <note>vinegar</note>, and strain it off. Mix this into the above-mentioned water, and put the water in a gilded cup. The Sol <note>gold</note> is dissolved from the silver and is again reduced with borax.

## THE SOFTENING OF IRON AND ALL METALS.

Take equal parts of alum, sal ammoniac, and tartar. Put them in good acetum <note>vinegar</note> over a fire and extinguish the metal in it.

### SOLUTION WITHOUT ANTIMONY.

Take Venus <note>copper</note> which has gold in it, and sprinkle on it the following powder: put it over a fire and let it melt. Then pour it into a fusibulum <note>casting mold or melting vessel</note> and you will find gold or Luna <note>silver</note>. Purify over ashes.

### ALSO.

Take one part of saltpetre with three parts of sulphur and proceed with copper as described above.

### WATER OF GRADATION.

Take two parts of vitriol, one part of alum, and half a part of antimony. Distill.

### FIXATION OF MERCURY.

Take a vessel, in which you put a sufficient quantity <note>*quant. suff.*</note> of quicklime, and in the middle of this lime place coagulated mercury. Heat for five hours, and it will be fixed.

### READY METHOD OF COAGULATION.

Take the pounded root and portions of the herb hermodactyl. Heat mercury, pour it over them, and it will be fixed.

### THE FIXATION OF ARSENIC.

Take equal parts of tartar, quicklime, glass, and arsenic. Soak <note>imbibe</note> with oil of tartar, and sublimate in a vessel after the usual method. When the whiteness ascends, stop.

### GILDING.

Stamped money is entirely gilded in the juice of the aurearia and remains so for some time.

### FIXATION OF SALTPETRE.

Take the purest saltpetre. Distill by means of an alembic and a portion of the saltpetre will remain at the bottom. Take one part of this and two parts of quicklime. Dissolve on stone, coagulate, and the process is complete.

### PERFECT FIXATION OF LUNA.

Take two parts of this saltpetre and one part of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note>. Let them melt. When the saltpetre becomes like glass, increase the fire until the saltpetre is consumed. Add <term>crocus of Mars</term> <note>iron oxide</note> and let it be consumed as before. Afterwards, pour it through antimony as is necessary, and let it be <term>fulminated</term> <note>purified in a furnace</note>. Then it will be <term>Luna</term> fixed and white.

### THE COAGULATION OF MERCURY, PRODUCING VENUS.

Take equal parts of Mercury and <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note> as much as you like. Boil them in water for three hours and stir continually. Afterwards, take the Mercury, put it into a linen rag, let it stand for a night, and it will be coagulated as <term>Venus</term>.

### ANOTHER COAGULATION OF MERCURY.

Take an egg-shaped crucible and fill it with mercury. Lute it <note>seal it with clay</note>, place it in a <term>patella</term> <note>a shallow pan or dish</note>, pour lead over it, and let it cool. Then take it out, and you have coagulated Mercury.

### PURIFICATION OF METALS.

Take two parts of antimony, and two parts each of vitriol and saltpetre. Pound well a moderate weight of filings from the metal, and cement over a slow fire for about an hour. Then let it be heated for 15 hours, and afterwards fulminated. It will be diminished by one-third part.

### CEMENT FROM ABOVE.

Take equal parts of saltpetre, sal ammoniac, verdigris, common salt, and alum. Pound them together and soak them three times with urine. Afterwards, with a portion of this, make layer upon layer for six hours, ending with a strong fire. Then you will have a golden <term>regulus</term> <note>the metallic part of a mineral</note>, but it will not stand in the <term>cineritium</term> <note>a cupellation hearth or refining furnace</note>.

### OIL WHICH TINGES LUNA INTO SOL.

Take antimony 5. j., with ½ lb. of sublimated Mercury. From this proceeds a red oil which has the property of gilding.

### OIL TINGING BRASS INTO GOLD OF 24 DEGREES.

Take the very strongest <term>lixivium</term> <note>lye or alkaline solution</note> and distill by means of a rose alembic. Then place it in a glass vessel and add saltpetre, sulphur, and <term>crocus of Mars</term> j. 3. or more, etc., so that the lixivium may float on the surface to the depth of one finger. Let it stand until it sinks to the bottom. This is done over a coal fire and it will become red like blood. Afterwards, take it from the fire and let it cool. Place it again in an alembic and distill it until whiteness appears. What remains at the bottom is a tincture, and is a most wonderful production, possessing the virtue of natural gold.

### PERFECT FIXATION OF LUNA.

Take cinnabar, rock salt <note>gem-salt</note>, and common salt. Pound them well with plates of silver <note>Luna</note>. Seal them <note>lute</note> layer on layer, place them on a cementing fire for six hours, then purify by cupellation <note><term>cineritium</term></note> and repeat this process three times. Afterwards, place them in cement for 18 hours and you have fixed silver.

Take three parts of this silver, one part of pure gold <note>Sol</note>, and dissolve them together. Its color is not diminished in nitric acid <note>aqua fortis</note>, but remains there.

### GLORIOUS OIL OF SOL.

Take very strong <term>lixivium</term> <note>lye</note> and distill it in an <term>alembic</term> with sulfur, <term>colcothar</term> <note>iron oxide residue</note>, and <term>crocus of Mars</term> <note>iron oxide</note>, using equal parts of each. Dissolve them in the lixivium, and afterwards place it on the fire, making it boil until it grows red. Next, distill it twelve times, or even more often, until a white substance comes forth. What remains at the bottom is a fixed oil and it tinges everything to the nature of gold <note>Sol</note>.

### ST. THOMAS AQUINAS.

I have very often sublimated Mercury until it became fixed. I afterwards dissolved it in water into its primal matter. In this water I placed the calx of silver <note>Luna</note> and fixed arsenic. This I now dissolved in horse manure and coagulated it, whereupon it became a stone of tincture.

### WATER OF MERCURY.

Take 3℔. 5. <note>3 pounds and 5 parts or ounces</note> of fixed Mercury, with the same quantity of saltpeter. Pulverize them together. Then place them in a linen cloth in horse manure, with glass underneath. Above all this, put a cloth as a covering, setting the horse manure on all sides, both above and below. Let it remain for two weeks, and then pound it until it is quite white. It will be sufficient for silver <note>Luna</note>.

### WATER OF SAL AMMONIAC.

Take sal ammoniac, the same quantity of eggshells, and a little <term>acetum</term> <note>vinegar</note>. Pound these together. Dissolve them afterwards on marble and you will have water of sal ammoniac.

### LAC VIRGINIS.

Take pulverized litharge, together with a sufficient quantity of <term>acetum</term>. Let them boil well. Afterwards, distill with a white filter. Pour it on again, and distill until the water grows clear. Then take some sal ammoniac and <term>anatron</term> <note>soda or natron</note>. Treat these in the same way, and afterwards mix them together. Then *lac virginis* <note>Virgin's Milk</note> is produced.

### PURGATION OF VENUS AFTER THE GREEK METHOD.

Dissolve copper <note>Venus</note> and project on it some purified sulfur or arsenic, until it no longer emits any smoke.

### FOR RECOVERING LUNA IN ANTIMONY.

Take 1 🜔 of Antimony and 2 🜔 of Tartar. Pound together with 3 parts of Sulfur. Pulverize, and melt.

### THE OPERATION BONI THEMATIS.

### THE OPERATION BONÆ RAPACIS.

### CALX PEREGRINORUM, OR MARINE CALX.

Take the bones of large fishes, or <term>signum peregrinorum</term> <note>scallop shells or pilgrim tokens</note>, or cockle shells. Reduce them to a calx, and when it has acquired whiteness you will have the "Calx of Pilgrims" <note>Calx Peregrinorum</note>.

### PAPUA TINCTURE.

Take as much distilled wine <note>vinum ardens</note> as is sufficient, and as much pounded antimony as you wish. Wash it in the usual way. Take the more subtle portion and project it upon dissolved silver <note>Luna</note>. It becomes in some part gold <note>Sol</note>, as I myself have seen.

### THE WORK OF THE NOBLE CANON IN ALCHEMY.

We have seen when we cemented <term>pars cum parte</term> <note>equal parts</note>, and the golden <term>regulus</term> <note>metallic mass</note> was placed in the cement, that the result was, as it were, the best gold. But it did not remain in the cupellation <note>cineritium</note> as equal parts. Nevertheless, it did remain in aqua fortis. Thus we made a cement on fixed silver <note>Luna</note>, and placed that silver in aqua fortis, at which point it deposited for us a large residue. When, however, this was <term>fulminated</term> <note>refined by intense heat</note>, it grew white again as silver. Once more we placed it in aqua fortis, and not the least thing remained for us in that aqua fortis. We believe that the matter in the cementations is either nothing at all, or is not cemented sufficiently, or its <term>realgar</term> <note>arsenic disulfide</note> is not fixed enough.

### CALCINATION OF ALL GEMS.

Take any quantity you like of each gem. Pulverize it and mix it with sulfur. Set fire to it; thus it burns, and you have the <term>calx</term> <note>powdery residue</note> of that gem. If it is necessary, wash it, and the powder will be white.

### HOW BONES MAY BE CUT.

Take wood ashes and quicklime in equal parts, *quant. suff.* <note>a sufficient quantity</note>. Boil the bones in this until they are softened.

### SOFTENING OF METALS AND IVORY.

Take the strongest <term>lixivium</term> <note>alkaline solution or lye</note> of alkali and place the metal in it for fourteen days, at which point it will be softened. Take it out again, cool it in water, and it will once more become hard. Treat ivory in the same way, having previously added the strongest <term>acetum</term> <note>vinegar</note>.

### TO GILD METALS.

Smear the metal with varnish, and then place upon it a plate of <term>Sol</term> <note>gold</note>.

### TO WHITEN VENUS.

Take <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note> and dissolve <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> in it. Then, with pounded tartar and common salt, make a pulp and dry it. Thus it can be used with <term>acetum</term> <note>vinegar</note>. Some add <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note>, smear the <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note>, and heat it, continuing the process until the result is satisfactory.

### LIGHT SHINING WITHOUT FIRE.

Take the eye of a goat, put it in water, and place a mirror above it.

### ANOTHER.

Take some <term>lixivium</term> <note>lye</note> made out of the best quicklime. Place alum and camphor within it. Put it in a glass vessel with live <term>Mercury</term> <note>quicksilver</note> and set a mirror above it.

### WATER OF COMMON SALT AND WATER OF SALTPETRE.

Take some of this with tile and distill it. This water is said to have a marvelous power of fixation. If <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> and common salt are melted in it, it can be distilled with honey.

### WHITE.

Take <term>alcalum</term> <note>an alkaline substance</note> with the juice of white onions. Steep <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note> in it, and it becomes <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note>.

### METHOD OF QUARTATION.

Take one part of <term>Sol</term> <note>gold</note>, and let two or three parts of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> be made into plates and put into <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note>. This is the most consummate and excellent test of gold.

### COLOURING.

Take a little <term>flos æris</term> <note>flower of copper or verdigris</note> and <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note>. Make them into a paste with <term>acetum</term> <note>vinegar</note>. It is one method of testing and coloring gold.

### HOW A CLOTH CANNOT BE BURNT IN THE FIRE.

Moisten the cloth with salt water. Let it dry by itself. Prepare it carefully with white of egg. Afterward dry it, and the effect is produced.

### WHEN GLASS IS BROKEN BY FIRE.

Take a half portion of minium, quicklime, and flour. Mix with the white of eggs. Apply a cloth moistened with it, and place it for a short time over the fire.

### LUTE.

Take ten parts of well-prepared lute, three parts of cows' hair, five parts of horse-dung, three parts of goat's blood, three parts each of quicklime and common salt, six parts of iron filings, and a sufficient quantity of white of egg and gypsum. This is how a lute is made.

### ANOTHER FOR SEALING BROKEN GLASS.

Take equal parts of calcined flint, quicklime, common salt, and white of eggs. Mix these together, then take a cloth, place it in the mixture, and smear the glass or the fracture. Let it harden; then smear it in water with linseed oil, and a better lute could scarcely be found.

### A VERY STRONG LUTE, WHICH IS PROOF AGAINST FIRE.

This is made out of bullock's blood, quicklime, and salt. It is indestructible in fire.

### AN EXCELLENT METHOD OF SEALING GLASS.

Take sufficient quantities of Venetian glass, finely pounded, and oil of tartar. Make a pulp; seal the fracture and place it before the fire to melt.

### TO MAKE MINIUM.

Take as much of <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note> as you please, dissolve it to ashes and it becomes citron-colored. Afterward, pound it, place it in a vessel over a moderate fire, and it will be colored red.

### THE PROCESS OF SULFUR.

Take 5. j. of this powder. Pour linseed oil over it, place it in an iron pan, and let it boil. It produces a red froth and grows thick. Pour it out and it becomes a red substance as thick as <term>hepar</term> <note>liver-colored mass</note>. Put the particles into which it is divided into an iron pan with <term>laterine oil</term> <note>oil of bricks</note> and boil it thoroughly for two hours. Afterward, place it in a glass vessel on ashes for three days. Then the sulfur is converted into an oil. Take the glass vessel again and put it in cold water for three days and three nights. Then distill it, first of all over a slow fire, but increasing the heat until it is sufficient. Thoroughly calcine the dregs, which are called the <term>caput mortuum</term> <note>the "dead head" or residue remaining after distillation</note>. Saturate it with the first water. Then distill for seven hours. Do this again until the redness of the oil is changed to white, which will take place in three hours. Finally, take the aforementioned oil again; distill it by itself for seven hours, and the process is complete.

Then take a plate of <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note> and dip it in the said oil. If it is transmuted into <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note>, well and good. If not, distill again until this takes place with the said calcined feces <note>dregs or sediment</note>.

### PREPARATION OF SALTS.

Make it with quicklime and by means of a <term>lixivium</term> <note>lye or alkaline solution</note>, as you know. Let it be soaked twice or thrice with oil of tartar, and the other also in oil of tartar.

### CONCERNING TALC.

Let it be cemented a whole day with common salt. Afterwards, let the talc be collected from the salt and very finely pounded. Let it be put in a bag. Let a very strong <term>lixivium</term> be poured over it. Let it be poured over again, until the <term>calx</term> is dissolved. Then it settles at the bottom of the <term>lixivium</term>. Dry it very well beforehand. Afterwards, let it be dissolved into oil. It coagulates <term>Mercury</term> into <term>Luna</term>, and similarly <term>Jupiter</term> <note>tin</note>.

### DIGESTION OF LUNA.

> Take Saltpetre, }
> Vitriol, } 1 lb. each.
> Cinnabar, 4 drachms (ʒiiij).

Make a "strong water" <note>aqua fortis</note>. Let this water be divided. In one part let there be <term>Luna</term>, and in the other cinnabar. Let them be dissolved by the addition of <term>sal ammoniac</term> and then joined together. Let them be digested for fourteen days and the matter distilled. Then let it be reduced, and you will have a double quantity of <term>Luna</term>. Each <term>loto</term> <note>a unit of weight, about half an ounce</note> of the salt will have a <term>loto</term> and a half.

### CONCERNING TALC.

Let it be cemented with common salt a whole day in <term>aqua-fortis</term>. Afterwards, the talc must be collected, very finely pounded, and put in a bag. Let it be melted over a very strong lye, and let the process be repeated until the talc is dissolved. It then settles at the bottom of the lye. Dry it well beforehand, then dissolve it into an oil. It coagulates <term>Mercury</term> into <term>Luna</term>, and <term>Jupiter</term> likewise.

### SEPARATION OF SOL AND LUNA.

> Take Antimony, 8 drachms (ʒviij).
> Filings of <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note>, 6 drachms (ʒvj).
> Crude Tartar, 4 drachms (ʒiiij).

Pound all together and fuse in a <term>tigillum</term> <note>crucible</note>. Then there will be a black substance, which you should also grind to a powder. Take equal parts of this and of <term>Luna</term>. Fuse the <term>Luna</term> with the powder until it appears bright and clear. Place it in a <term>cupel</term> with lead, and the antimony entirely evaporates. Afterwards, purge it by means of a <term>cineritium</term> <note>a refining furnace or cupellation process</note>.

### CONCERNING SCORIA OF LUNA.

Take <term>scorias</term> <note>dross or slag</note> and powders in equal quantities. Melt them until you have refined the silver. Let this process be thoroughly carried out, then refine it.

### THE FIXATION OF CINNABAR IN ONE DAY.

Take 8 parts of beech ashes and 1 part of quicklime. Make a <term>lixivium</term> <note>an alkaline solution or lye</note>, in which you dissolve 1 part each of salt nitre, salt of vitriol, and verdigris; and half a part each of flower of alum and calcined tartar. Dissolve these; boil the cinnabar in this for a whole day, and it will be fixed.

### ON ANTIMONY.

Soak the mineral in <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>. Afterwards, scatter sand upon it. Then the sand attracts the antimony to itself. When it becomes <term>scoria</term> <note>slag or dross</note>, remove it with a spatula and sprinkle sand again, as before, until it will no longer evaporate. Then fulminate <note>refine or react with heat</note>.

### CONCERNING THE SOLUTION OF MAGNESIA.

Take one part of it and 2 parts of sublimated <term>Mercury</term>. Grind, mix them together, and distill using an <term>alembic</term>. Then a thick and fatty water, like linseed oil, is distilled. This tinges <term>Mercury</term> within itself. Then it tinges all bodies cast into it.

### FIXATION OF ANTIMONY.

Melt them together, then let them stand to cool, and the antimony will be fixed.

->1 lb. of Antimony<-

### OIL OF BORAX.

Put borax into a glass vessel and dissolve it. Let it be pulverized, hardened, and placed inside another glass vessel in a <term>balneum Mariæ</term> <note>a water bath</note>. It is converted into an oil which fixes all spirits.

### OIL OF GOLD.

->Take 1 part of Sulphur<-
->8 parts of Quicklime<-

### WATER OF ANTIMONY (SULPHUR) FOR SOL.

Grind it, and take 3 parts of it, with one part of <term>sal ammoniac</term>. Place it within a glass vessel, well sealed, on ashes for one day. ### FIXATION OF SULPHUR.

Take sulphur and honey. Soak and dry over a slow fire. Then let it boil well in a strong <term>lixivium</term>. Wash the substance until the water appears clear. Renew this process seven times, and you will find the sulphur white like crystal. Afterwards take prepared common salt and the same quantity of <term>sal ammoniac</term> and sulphur. Let these be well ground together twice. Then dissolve with white of egg, and congeal. Distill by means of a filter, and cool. Repeat this three times, and 1 part changes 30 parts of warmed mercury into permanent <term>Luna</term>.

### FIXED OIL OF SULPHUR.

Take it, let it boil in alkali for one day, and be sublimated over a slow fire. Having done this, moisten it with <term>acetum</term> four times, abstract by means of a filter, and again moisten three times. It is afterwards abstracted by means of an <term>alembic</term>, and will then be fixed. Let it be dissolved into an oil on marble. Then take the body of the sulphur, dissolve it with oil, and congeal. One part transforms three parts to <term>Luna</term>, and that <term>Luna</term> has many of the properties of gold.

### THE WHITENING AND FIXATION OF CINOBRIUM.

Take it, together with calcined alum and prepared common salt. Pound together with <term>vinum ardens</term> <note>distilled wine or alcohol</note>, dry, and sublimate. Then it is whitened and fixed.

### FIXATION OF SPIRITS.

Take quicklime, alkali salt, and oil mixed with them. Distill, and saturate the spirits with test water, repeating the process until it melts on the plate.

### WATER OF MERCURY FIXING ALL SPIRITS.

->Take 1 mark of Mercury.<-
->Take 2 marks of Sal Ammoniac.<-

Rub the two together in a glass vessel over a slow fire, and it will become a hard mass. Grind this, and it will become a powder, which you should dissolve in water. Then take 1 mark of pure <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> or <term>Sol</term> <note>gold</note> carefully made into plates. Put this in the mentioned water; and this water fixes all spirits.

### TO FUSE BONES.

Take any quantity of bones and burn them into lime. Having done this, carefully grind it. Take 4 lbs. of this and 1/2 lb. of quicklime. Mix them together in the powder. Afterwards, dissolve some bitumen in a moderate quantity of wine until all of it has melted away. Then place the bones in it, and stir briskly into a thick pulp. Afterwards, pour it into a mould made of paper. First, however, let it be smeared with oil; set it to cool, and it will harden like ivory. During the process of fusion, you can give it any color with <term>minium</term> <note>red lead</note>, *flos æris* <note>verdigris or "flower of copper"</note>, or any other tints you like.

### TO MAKE A MOULD FOR CASTING ALL KINDS OF IMAGES.

Grind tiles very fine and boil them in strong <term>lixivium</term> <note>an alkaline solution or lye</note> so that they form an exceedingly thin paste. Dry this and strain it carefully. Afterwards, make a liquid from the whites of eggs. Then let it be pressed in a machine, and it will dry from the top.

### TO COLOUR GLASS.

Take tartar, wood ashes, and quicklime. Make an alkali from them. Take 1 part of it and dissolve it in 3 parts of color in water (*sic*). Coagulate it, and again dissolve it with the color. Do this three or four times until the stone is thoroughly colored. Afterwards, melt glass with the mentioned stone. It will be colored by the stone, and in this way you can fuse crystal.

### A METHOD OF COLOURING WHEREBY SOFTENED CRYSTAL CAN BE TINTED AND HARDENED LIKE A PRECIOUS STONE.

Take 1 part of alkali made from tartar, 1/2 part of sublimated <term>salmiax</term> <note>sal ammoniac</note>, and 2 parts of color. Grind them well together, dissolve in water, and again pour the color upon it, repeating the process until the color is sufficiently deep. Then it will be coagulated into a stone. Grind this very fine and mix it with a crystal that has been previously softened with oil of tartar. The red color is made with cinnabar and becomes equally red with it; the citron-color is made from saffron, and the green with sap-green.

## HOW EVERY STONE CAN BE TRANSMUTED INTO A CLEAR ONE, THOUGH IT BE ITSELF OPAQUE, AND WHEREBY YOU CAN TINGE A BODY, BOTH CRYSTAL AND ALL SIMILAR BODIES. EXAMPLE.

Take of <term>hematite</term> stone, very finely ground, 2 parts. Let it boil fiercely in a <term>lixivium</term> <note>an alkaline solution or lye</note> (previously prepared from tartar, wood ashes, and quicklime) for half a day, so that it may be alkalized. Then sprinkle over it 3 parts each of both sublimated <term>sal ammoniac</term> and crude <term>sal ammoniac</term>. Dry it over a very slow fire. Afterward, dissolve it in water in a damp cellar, and whatever remains on the stone, soak it again with that water, repeating the operation until the whole is turned into oil. Then put it into a glass vessel and <term>sublimate</term> from the oil itself the <term>sal ammoniac</term> which is not fixed. When you see it has ascended and is no longer in the oil, then grind the stone and boil it still further in the <term>lixivium</term> for six or eight hours; and then again, as before, dissolve it with the <term>sal ammoniac</term>, both sublimated and crude. Then, by the sublimation of the <term>lixivium</term> and the solution of the <term>sal ammoniac</term>, it is changed into a thick oil. Then those spirits which are not fixed are separated from it, such as the <term>sal ammoniac</term> by sublimation, in the way specified before. The <term>lixivium</term> will not be separated; but add water, which has been distilled by a filter; then the oil will remain at the bottom, and the <term>lixivium</term> will be raised up with the water. Thus it will be separated, and you will have the oil of the stone alone. It is better, however, not to separate the alkali, but to let it remain in the oil.

### DESCRIPTION OF THE ADEPT'S FIRE.

->Take Vitriol, }<-
->Alum, } 1 lb. each.<-
->Saltpetre, }<-
->Calcined Alum, }<-
->Calcined Vitriol, } ½ lb. each.<-

Distill in <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note> for 30 hours. Afterwards take 2 lbs. of the following strong water:
->Calcined Alum, }<-
->Calcined Vitriol, } 1 lb. each.<-
->Saltpetre, 1½ lb.<-

Distill as above and renew three times. Having done this, dissolve in the following strong water:
->Sal Ammoniac, 2 quarts.<-
-><term>Salmiax</term>, 1 quart.<-
->Sublimated Mercury, 1 [part].<-
->Calcined Tartar and its Alkali (*no quantity given*).<-
->Sublimated Arsenic, 1 quart.<-

After each has been separately dissolved, let it be distilled by a [water] bath and poured over twice. Afterwards, let it be hardened a little and dissolve in a moist bath into a water. In this water, dissolve 3 parts of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note>, or as much as will dissolve. Coagulate into a hard stone and let this boil in a very strong <term>lixivium</term> into most potent water until it is alkalized. Dissolve and coagulate as long as you please.

### Oil of Sulphur.

### NOTE.

Place verdigris in ashes so that it may turn white. Then quench it in vinegar, and it will become red. Afterward, grind it, wash it thoroughly, and dry it again. <term>Tutty</term> <note>zinc oxide</note> is prepared in the same way and becomes red. Also take 2 oz. of <term>crocus of Mars</term> <note>iron oxide</note>. Wash it in the manner of <term>ceruse</term> <note>white lead</note>. Take the finer portion. Dry it and saturate it with vinegar. In this way, dry twice that which floats on top.

Also take:
Of <term>Crocus of Mars</term>, 1 oz.
Of <term>Tutty</term>, 1 oz.
Of Verdigris, 1 oz.
Of Vitriol, prepared as above, 1 oz.

Mix these together, grinding them well.

Place these in a <term>tigillum</term> <note>crucible</note> well luted <note>sealed with clay</note>. Let it stand twelve hours in flux <note>molten state</note>. Afterwards, cool it down and fulminate the <term>regulus</term> <note>the metallic mass, here called "the king"</note> with the same quantity of <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>. You will then find 12 <term>lotones</term> <note>units of weight, approximately half-ounces</note> of fixed <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note> from one pound. It makes no more <term>scoria</term> <note>slag or dross</note>, nor is it further destroyed by Mercury. You can make it red or white.

### TO THE WHITE WITH METALLIC ARSENIC.
Let it be fixed by means of saturation with the oil of eggs and of tartar until the tincture is made.

### <term>CROCUS OF MARS</term> <note>a red oxide of iron</note>.
Take any quantity of <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note>, and the same of saltpeter. Make it burn and become red. Let it also become sulphur, etc. Also take 1.5 ounces of sal ammoniac. Pound it. Also take 2 ounces of glass, prepared and pounded as described above. Mix and soak with vinegar twice. Also take 4 ounces of filings of <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note> and two ounces of red vitriol. Make <term>crocus</term> with vinegar, as you have seen. Let the oil of <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note> be distilled. Soak the sal ammoniac as before until it turns red. Take 1 lb. of antimony, well pounded, and 1 lb. of tartar. Mix well. Next, dry it. Shut it up in a jar, so that it does not turn white on the coals. Leave it for two hours. Afterwards, pound it and pour <term>vinum ardens</term> <note>strong distilled alcohol</note> over it, so that it is saturated. Place it in a phial for a night and a day. Next, distill it. Pour it over again, and distill by a slow fire.

### TO SOFTEN GLASS.
Take <term>Lybisticum</term> <note>lovage</note>. Press out the sap. Cause the glass to boil in this.

### THIS IS THE METHOD OF MAKING <term>LUNA</term> <note>silver</note>.
Take 1 lb. of Mercury. Heat it, and pour over it the following water: Take 1 lb. of common salt and 1 quart of saltpeter. Grind them, and then bake 1 quart of lime. Mix well in an iron dish over a slow fire until it froths, for one hour. Remove from the fire and cool. Mix everything together, and dip it into oil twice. Fulminate this Mercury in a <term>cineritium</term> <note>refining furnace or cupel</note>, and you will rejoice forever.

### CORRECTION OF OIL OF TARTAR, FOR BEAUTY AND FOR <term>LUNA</term> <note>silver</note>.
Arrange tartar and lime layer upon layer. Burn them well. Then filter for two hours. Lastly, dissolve them, and you will have corrected oil of tartar.

### NOTE.
Take equal parts of sulphur and Mercury. Form a paste like an amalgam. Then mix with salt. Let them remain in a gentle state of flux for about half an hour. Then burn them; afterwards, wash them. Grind the Mercury which you find there with a salve of <term>Aza</term> <note>likely asafoetida</note>, wax, <term>vinum ardens</term> <note>strong distilled alcohol</note>, etc., until it is burnt. Finally, reduce it in a <term>cineritium</term> <note>refining furnace or cupel</note> with borax, and you will have <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> without any doubt.

### **NOTE.** FOR MAKING ICE EASILY MELTED IN FIRE, AND SUCH ALSO AS IS NOT DISSOLVED BY WATER.

Take aquafortis made from saltpetre and alum, together with oil of tartar, 1 lb. each. Pour all together; then put into them a little vinum ardens <note>burning wine or alcohol</note>, and the whole will coagulate into an ice by the power of fire.

### OIL WHICH WE USE FOR PROJECTION ON MELTED LUNA.

->Take Purest Gold, 1 loth.<-
->Sal Ammoniac, 4 loth.<-
->Oil of Antimony, 10 loth.<-
->Aquafortis, *a sufficient quantity*<-

Dissolve, as you know how. Having done this, let it putrefy for seven days, and distill by a bath, continually renewing the whole until the aforesaid materials are converted into a thick oil. Of this take 10 loth, with 2 loth of the purest gold. Dissolve at the same time 4 loth each of sublimated Mercury and fixed sublimated sal ammoniac. Proceed as above with fresh aquafortis, and all these ingredients are converted into a thick oil. In this oil, dissolve as much gold as possible. The oil will then transmute into gold all metals on which it is projected, and if it is coagulated into a stone, it colors it beyond measure. By this method, you can proceed to silver. Mercury will be fixed with white of eggs, and in the same manner sal ammoniac.

### A WONDERFUL CEMENT BY ONE STONE OVER LUNA.

->Take Crocus of Mars, 1 loth.<-
->Hæmatite, 2 loth.<-
->Verdigris, 5 loth.<-

Having done so, take 1/2 lb. of this alkali, 4 loth of sal ammoniac, and 1 loth of sublimated salmiax <note>sal ammoniac</note>. Mix together and dissolve on marble into a watery oil. Pour the oil thus made on the dregs, and keep doing this until the whole matter is turned into water. This being done, coagulate it into a stone, which you must sublimate in order that the sal ammoniac may evaporate, and the matter alone may remain. Then once more boil the stone in very strong red lixivium. Again add the aforesaid weight, dissolve into oil, and again coagulate the oil, sublimate the sal ammoniac from it, and do this over and over again until the substance of the ingredients flows from them on the marble. Take this water, coagulate it afresh, dissolve it again and put it in 1 quartal of powder or 1 loth of water of ducat-gold. When it is dissolved, coagulate it. This stone is effective in cements, and effective also in projections. It also colors crystal.

### ANTIMONY.

Let them be melted until the water ceases to redden and the antimony becomes white. Put the froth in a glass. Coagulate it. ### CROCUS OF MARS.

Dissolve in <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note>. Then distill the <term>aquafortis</term> from there. Distill the solution through a filter, and then cause the <term>acetum</term> to evaporate. Afterwards strengthen the fire. ### WATER OF MERCURY.

Take 1 lb. of crude Mercury. Put it in a cucurbit <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel</note> to distill. Use a slow fire, and a single drop will come forth. Pour this back; distill again, and two drops will come forth. Pour these back again, and continue this process until the whole is converted into water. This water penetrates and dissolves bodies.

### NOTE.

Take crude tartar and pound it well. Then distill through an alembic. Pour its water again upon the dregs, and distill again until a water or oil collects; then put the same into another receptacle. Afterward rectify it. Take live calx <note>quicklime</note> in the same quantity as red oil. Pound it thoroughly. Then extract the water through the alembic until no more dregs remain at the bottom. Next put half as much sulfur into the oil. Putrefy for ten days. Afterwards again distill. Then make an amalgam out of one part of Luna <note>silver</note> and five parts of Mercury. Heat and extinguish in oil six times. Then Mercury is fixed, and there are many <term>arcana</term> <note>alchemical secrets or mysteries</note> in it.

### NOTE.

The calx of the body is cast into a flux of saltpeter over the fire. Dissolve it in a cold chamber. It falls on the bodies.

### WATER OF LUNA.

Make an <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note> from one pound of saltpetre and two pounds of vitriol. Dissolve half an ounce of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> in it; then dissolve common salt in warm water. Pour the <term>aquafortis</term> containing the <term>Luna</term> into the salt water, and it will be precipitated. Then draw the water off from it and dry the precipitate. Add one ounce of sugar-candy to the dissolved half ounce. Pour a fresh supply of <term>aquafortis</term> upon it again. Extract the moisture from it in a bath. Afterward, place it in a sand <term>cupel</term> <note>a shallow porous cup used in refining</note> and extract the water of the moon through the <term>alembic</term> <note>a distillation apparatus</note>. If it does not rise more than once, pour the distilled water back over it until all of it has passed through.

### THE FIXATION OF ARSENIC.

Take two parts of alum and one part of saltpetre. Make a liquid by means of an <term>alembic</term>, and put one part of sublimated arsenic into that liquid. Distill it until it becomes a fixed water.

### FIXATION OF MERCURY.

->Take of Fixed Arsenic, }<-
->of Sal Ammoniac, } two parts each.<-
->of Fixed Sulphur, one part.<-

Melt them together. Then take one <term>marc</term> <note>a unit of weight, about 8 ounces</note> of Mercury. Warm it. Next, put it into the melted mixture. Wait one hour. Then refine it in <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note> on the <term>test</term> <note>a refining vessel</note>. You will lose nothing, and you will have more than two parts of the <term>Sun</term> <note>gold</note>. You may then also take the Mercury which is coagulated with the smoke of <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>.

### TRUE ALBATIO.

->Take of Sublimated <term>Zaibach</term> <note>mercury</note>, 10 parts.<-
->White Sublimated <term>Kybrick</term> <note>arsenic or sulfur</note>, 3 parts.<-
->Sal Ammoniac, 3 parts.<-

Moisten these frequently with water of sal ammoniac, and dry them until they are white and roasted. Moisten and roast them again. Finally, take "water of the eagle"—that is, sal ammoniac—in double the amount of the powders. Put it to dissolve under moderately warm dung for three weeks. Then take it out of the dung and congeal it into white powders. Project one part of these onto 100 parts of purified <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note>, and the whole will become silver. These are the truest experiments of many philosophers who have worked with <term>Zaibach</term>, <term>Kybrick</term>, and the "eagle." For these are three great spirits. Thus prepared, they transform metals.

### TO FIX SULPHUR.

Take as much <term>aquafortis</term> as you wish. Add one ounce of native sulphur and the same quantity of pulverized alum. Dissolve these in water, and the sulphur will become red as blood and fixed. This water dissolves all bodies.

### NOTE.

Mercury is called honey, calcined <term>Luna</term>, or "the assistance." Water of Mercury is simply called "water." Thus says Plato.

### FIXING SALT.

Take 2 parts <term>quicklime</term>.
1 part soft <term>smegma</term> <note>a soapy or cleansing substance</note>.
½ part wood ashes.

Also some ashes from the dregs of wine <note>tartar</note>. Reduce all these to powder so that they may become a strong <term>lixivium</term> <note>a solution of alkaline salts; lye</note>. Strain through a filter; coagulate, and you will have fixing salt, concerning which see below also.

### FIXING OIL.

Take three parts of olive oil, two parts of <term>quicklime</term>, and one part of <term>sal ammoniac</term>. Mix all together and distill the oil from them. Do this three times, always renewing the dregs.

### SOFT SOAP.

Take twelve <term>scutellæ</term> <note>small bowls or dishes</note> of water, in which place one <term>scutella</term> of wood ashes. Boil until dissolved. Then add half a <term>scutella</term> and boil until the water is reduced by one-third. Remove from the fire and distill through a filter. Then, to two parts of the water thus strained off, add a third part of oil. Do this by evaporating over a fire.

### COAGULATION OF MERCURY.

Make an amalgam from one part of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> and five parts of purified <term>Mercury</term>. Place it in a glass vessel with a narrow neck which is well-smeared below with the <term>lute of wisdom</term> <note>a hermetic sealant made of clay and other materials</note>. Place one layer of the salt previously prepared under the amalgam in the glass, and another layer above. Afterwards, pour the oil previously prepared over it to the height of three fingers, and let it boil over a slow fire for seven days.

### NOTE.

In the art, we find two co-operators by whose means our work is more easily fulfilled. One is the destroyer, which is to say, <term>sal ammoniac</term>. But <term>sulphur</term> and <term>arsenic</term> reduced to an oil promote the work. The property of <term>sulphur</term> is to coagulate <term>Mercury</term>. But the property of <term>arsenic</term> is only to inspire and vivify the stone, if it is prepared in the proper manner. Hence, whoever omits the preparation of the oil of <term>Mercury</term> should take the oil of <term>arsenic</term> in its place. But when a philosopher speaks of joining the body and the spirit in matrimony by <term>sal ammoniac</term>, he speaks of the oil extracted from <term>Mercury</term>.

### SOLUTION OF BODIES.

Dissolve honey over a fire, and pour it over heated and crushed tiles so that they absorb the moisture. Then distill by an <term>alembic</term>, and a saffron-colored water will be produced, because otherwise the honey cannot be distilled. Into this water let the spirits of <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note> enter—that is to say, equal parts of <term>vitriol</term> and <term>saltpetre</term>. Then dissolve <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> and <term>Sol</term> <note>gold</note> in that water, and also prepare an ounce of processed common salt. Then this converted material can be eaten or drunk without injury, because it is <term>aurum potabile</term> <note>potable or drinkable gold</note>.

### NOTA BENE.
#### THAT YOU MAY KNOW THE RECIPE FOR SOLUTION.

Take a clean cloth, like ticking or fustian, as much as an ell <note>a unit of length, approximately 45 inches</note> in length; pour on it a pint of good wine, and with the wine mix about a half pint of good brandy. Tear the fustian or the cloth at first into fragments. Let it remain thus for three days. Afterwards, take it out and dry it on a board. When it has dried, take one piece after another on a small stick. Burn it as if to make tinder. Put the burnt pieces one by one into a brass basin. Place it in a cellar, where the whole will quickly become an oil. Then amalgamate <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> or <term>Sol</term> <note>gold</note> with three parts of <term>Mercury</term>. Let the <term>Mercury</term> evaporate again. Place a calx <note>a powdery metallic oxide</note> upon the stone slab. Pound it with brandy. Then take twice the quantity of the oil mentioned above, and twice the quantity of the body of <term>Mercury</term>. Mix it thoroughly on a table made of <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>. Subsequently, set it in a moist place, where you will soon find the oil of the body, which you should use as you know how.

### LUNA FIXED BY ME.

Take saltpeter, antimony, and arsenic, and saturate them well with oil of tartar, so that they may be thoroughly mixed. Dry them somewhat. Afterwards, melt them in a *tigillum* <note>a crucible</note>, first over a slow fire and then over a stronger one. Pound the whole together into powders. Take of these one-fifth to one loth <note>a unit of weight, roughly half an ounce</note>, or more if you like, and you have, etc. (as written).

<term>Sol</term> <note>gold</note> is the primary substance which is not altered by fire; indeed, it is improved by fire, and cannot otherwise become a great or perfect elixir, which is of eternal duration, the rectifier and lightener of all bodies, and is joined with <term>Mars</term> <note>iron</note> and <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>. But it cannot be joined with <term>Mars</term> unless the <term>Mars</term> is filed into shavings; however, with <term>Saturn</term> it is joined as it is.*

### A NOBLE WORK.

Take <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note> and melt it. Before it hardens, add an equal amount of <term>Mercury</term>. Wash this amalgam thoroughly with water and salt, and afterwards with pure water. Grind it on a stone, and afterwards add as much sal ammoniac as there is <term>Mercury</term>. Place it in a damp, warm place. When it is entirely dissolved, take sublimated arsenic. Saturate it by pounding it thoroughly on the stone with the previously mentioned water. Set it to dissolve, but remember that there should be something there to lighten it. Let it stand until it is quite cold. This preparation serves as a means of lightening when it is added to one hundred parts of <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note> and to two hundred parts of <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>. But note that you ought to always place in it salt of alkali, so that the spirit may penetrate better and enter through the entire body.

### FIXATION AND RUBIFICATION OF MERCURY.

Take bloodstone, mix it with sal ammoniac, and sublimate it. Then the sal ammoniac ascends as a red vapor, but the stone will remain at the bottom, black. Then, having once sublimated the <term>Mercury</term>, grind it with that sal ammoniac and sublimate it again. The <term>Mercury</term> will remain at the bottom, fused and red.

### NOTE.

Calcine the cinnabar well with vitriol and salt, until it all transforms into the metal.

### NOTE.

Regarding whatever will not readily enter into lead, with nothing having been taken out, boil the materials in strong alkali. Add to it as much vitriol as you like, and it will enter in.

### WATER OF MERCURY.

Take four ounces each of sublimated mercury and of antimony. Break each into pieces separately. Put them together in a well-sealed <note>luted</note> retort. Place it in a sand bath; apply a gentle fire. Distill it over. Should it attach itself in the tube, loosen it with a hot coal. Increase the fire until nothing more comes over. When it is cold, put the matter upon a stone. Pound it into small pieces. If any mercury still remains, remove it. Then put it back into a retort. Distill it more effectively than before, until all the mercury has turned into water. In this way, you may also make oil of antimony. Take the material in a glass. Pound it small. Pound in the moisture. Do this continually and distill until a red oil comes over.

### FIXATION.

->Take one part of Mercury Sublimate.<-
->Two parts of Sulphur.<-

Break them up together. Put them in a cucurbit <note>a gourd-shaped boiling flask</note>. Place it in a sand bath. Let the odor be released, weak at first, then stronger. If the sulphur does not lose its smell, stir it with a piece of wood; it will then lose its smell quickly.

### PROOF.

Place it upon a plate. If it does not smell, it is fixed; if it does, take equal quantities of sulphur and mercury. Pound them together as before until it is fixed.

### REDUCE AS FOLLOWS.

Take one part each of litharge and of mercury, and a small quantity of sulphur. Put the mercury into the crucible and seal it thoroughly. Apply a small fire at first, then a stronger one, until it melts. Afterward, let it cool. Wash the <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note>. Refine it in <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note>. Then separate it in aquafortis <note>nitric acid</note>.

### WHITE.

Take the whites of forty eggs, beat them well and boil them. Then distill the water through a cloth. Afterward, take one pound of mercury sublimate and the same quantity of arsenic. Mix into a paste <note>impaste</note> frequently with the aforementioned water, and dry sufficiently. Afterward (according to another copy), let one pound of sal ammoniac be added twice. Pour the water over the pounded powder to a depth of one or two fingers. Place it in horse dung in a closed glass vessel for fifteen days. Take it out on the sixteenth day, and you will find a watery mass. Coagulate this in hot ashes <note>cinders</note>. One part of this tinges one hundred parts of the metals <note>bodies</note>, and especially of purified <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note>; if three or four parts of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note> are added to this, it will become perfect <term>Luna</term>. If you add a ferment, the <term>Luna</term> will be even more perfect.

### OIL OF MERCURY AND OF THE SUN FOR GILDING.

Take ½ oz. of Sal Ammoniac and 1 quint <note>a unit of weight</note> of Mercury Sublimate, which are to be well ground together. Put these into a hard-boiled egg from which the yolk has been removed. Make a small hole through the bottom of the shell with the quill of a pen. Place the egg on a small glass to allow the liquid to drain out. Do the same with the calx of the Sun <note>gold powder</note>. Take one quarter of the Sun. Paint it with Mercury. Put crushed salt into it. Let the Mercury lose its odor. Boil the salt with hot water from the calx. Then take twice as much sal ammoniac as there is calx. Put this also in an egg with a small hole. Set it as before to dissolve into an oil; but should the sal ammoniac not melt readily, moisten it with brandy.

### OIL OF VITRIOL.

Pour aquafortis <note>nitric acid</note> carefully over calcined vitriol. Let it stand to decompose for fourteen days. Afterward, let the watery part <note>phlegma</note> of the aquafortis be removed, and the oil will remain at the bottom.

### TO EXTRACT THE QUINTESSENCE OF LUNA, SATURN, OR JOVE.

Put tartar and sal ammoniac into acetum <note>vinegar</note> in a well-closed glass vessel. Put into this the ashes of Saturn <note>lead</note>, Jove <note>tin</note>, or Luna <note>silver</note>. Seal it thoroughly and set it in warm dung for eight days. Afterward distill it; the vinegar comes over first, and next the quintessence of the calx, in the manner of quicksilver.

### AQUAFORTIS ON VENUS, TO MAKE LUNA.

| Ingredient | Quantity |
| :--- | :--- |
| Salt | 1 lb. |
| Hungarian White Vitriol | 1 lb. |
| Alum | 1 lb. |
| Arsenic | 1 lb. |

Grind these into small pieces in the proper manner. Make aquafortis. Dissolve as much Venus <note>copper</note> as you like within it, and you will have silver in the quantity of one-half the amount.

### ELIXIR.

Take equal parts of Sol <note>gold</note>, Luna <note>silver</note>, Mars <note>iron</note>, and Venus <note>copper</note>. Melt them and make them into plates, which you should suspend over vinegar. Scrape off the green layer that forms there. Do this until the plates are entirely consumed and turned into green matter. A portion of this green on 10 parts of Luna transmutes it into the appearance of Sol. If you wash this green with warm water and afterward mix it with some water of sal ammoniac, letting it stand for seven days to dissolve, its effect is doubled. If, also, in place of sal ammoniac you added aqua foetida, which is Mercury, and then operated as you did with the water of sal ammoniac, you would confirm your work; nor can you make any mistake, because the metallic substances are combined in a philosophical way. Note this well.

### ANOTHER.

Redden <note>rubify</note> vitriol, grind it, and dissolve it in vinegar. Then sublimate sal ammoniac over a slow fire, and add what has been sublimated to the aforementioned red matter.

### THE FIXATION OF ORPIMENT.

Pound it and mix it with crepine oil. Pound it again, soak it, dry it, and pound it over a stone. Preserve it for use. Then put it in the fire and melt it. ### THE WORK OF ONE DAY FOR THE RED.

Take 5 parts of * and grind in a brass mortar with 1 part of sulphur. Place this in a vessel, sealed for four hours in a baker’s oven. Afterward, pound and soak it with water of atramentum <note>vitriol or blackening</note> and of sal ammoniac. Of this, project 1 part onto 30 parts of Luna <note>silver</note>, and thus it will be colored. If you melt this Luna with Sol <note>gold</note>, it will be very good.

### ANOTHER FOR SATURN.

->Take Pure Live Sulphur, 1 part.<-
->Crude Mercury, 2 parts.<-
->Prepared Vitriol, 2 oz.<-

First of all, join the sulphur with the vitriol, pulverized in vinegar over a slow fire so that it may be dissolved. Next, add Mercury by well-incorporating it with them and stirring it with a rod. Then it will be a black amalgam. Take this from the fire and grind it to an impalpable powder. Place it in a glass vessel well-luted <note>sealed with clay</note> with a good seal. Give it a moderate heat for two weeks. Then increase the fire for one week. Break the glass and pound it, giving it continuous heat until you have a bright red color. Then cool and pound it, placing it in another great and strong vessel, well-luted in the middle and closed with its hermetic seal. Give it a very strong fire for one week, until you see the substance melted like wax or oil. Then cool and take out that most precious substance. If it does not turn to oil as is here described, dissolve it with rectified aqua vitae and coagulate it three or four times until the oil remains in the fire. Then melt 8 lbs. of Saturn <note>lead</note> and 8 lbs. of Mercury. Make an amalgam, as you know how, by fusion, and project 1 lb. of this medicine, leaving it to melt for a quarter of an hour while mixing it with wood. Afterward, cool the black substance; one part of it tinges the 8 lbs. of Saturn and the 8 lbs. of Mercury into a medicine. Melt again 8 lbs. of Saturn and 8 lbs. of Mercury. Take one part of this medicament, do again as above, and you will find Sol <note>gold</note>.

### AUGMENTATION FOR SOL.

Take Saturn <note>lead</note>. Melt it and pour over it an equal quantity of Mercury. Then take the same quantity of white arsenic. Mix it with Saturn and Mercury, and let it become a powder. Then take three parts of Luna <note>silver</note>. Melt in *. Inject the powder gradually, and little by little, until it completely enters. Stir it well with a stick. Then purge in a cineritium <note>a cupeling furnace or ash-vessel used for refining</note>.

### A SECRET FOR THE SOLUTION OF SOL OR LUNA.

Pound thoroughly the calx <note>powdered oxide</note> of Luna <note>silver</note> or Sol <note>gold</note> with sal ammoniac. Place it in a glass vessel with the mouth open over hot ashes, and dry it with a moderate heat until a white mass is seen in which there is no plated Luna. Next, place it in dung or a bath of Mary <note>bain-marie</note> for nine or twelve natural days. Thus it is dissolved into water, which you should putrefy for the proper time. Afterward, congeal and dissolve it; and thus you will have the Stone.

### OIL OF TARTAR WHICH DISSOLVES ITSELF IN HEAT.

Take calcined tartar, or, as I think better, salt of tartar. Pour over it rectified water of life <note>aqua vitæ</note>. Let it stand 24 hours in the bath. Extract the water from it, and add fresh *aqua vitæ* continually. Let it putrefy for 24 hours, as before, and extract it. Do this until it dissolves itself into an oil. ### AUGMENT.

Take of Filings of Luna <note>silver</note>, ½ oz.

Amalgamate them. Add a third part of sublimated Mercury. Place in a jar or glass. Pour on oil of tartar so as to stand higher than two fingers' depth. Shut it up; place over a fire, and apply a slow heat for six days, until the matter is hardened. Take it out. Pound it on a stone. Place it again in the vessel. Add more oil as before. Set it again over a slow fire of five or six coals. Rule the fire for three days and it will be fixed. Then test it. Refine a small quantity in Saturn <note>lead</note>, but what you do not reduce, augment with Mercury and work as before.

### OIL OF TARTAR IS MADE AS FOLLOWS.

Dissolve calcined tartar in good wine vinegar. Distill through the filter. Cause the vinegar to evaporate. Dissolve again, doing so ten times. At length, permit the salt to melt by itself into an oil, which you should use for the above digestion.

### OIL OF LUNA.

Take of Verdigris, }
of Sulphur, } 2 oz. each.

Pound them, and place them in a glass cucurbit. From them, make a water like an aqua-fortis, with a gentle fire at first, and latterly with a stronger one. Next, take 2 oz. of Luna <note>silver</note> dissolved in common aqua-fortis. Pour the former water upon it. Extract the water together with the aqua-fortis through the alembic even unto the oiliness <note>original: olitet</note>, and the matter becomes brown in the glass; thus the Luna in the <unclear>Keldt</unclear> becomes hard, and melts in the warmth like an oil or wax. To the same Luna add 8 oz. of purged Mercury <note>☿</note>. Place in a cucurbit of glass and seal it well.

### FOR THE ASHES OF LUNA.

Place Luna <note>silver</note> in a crucible to melt, and when it is in a state of flux, cast salt of alkali upon it, thus purifying it. Then make filings from it and calcine them in an open reverberatory furnace for six days. In this way the salt is extracted; coagulate this and then dissolve it again. One part of it coagulates and fixes 40 parts of Mercury, and that Mercury, once coagulated, tints 50 parts of purified Venus <note>copper</note> into real gold.

### OIL OF SULPHUR.

Take Sulphur, )
Tartar, ) 1 lb. each.
Glassgall <note>scum from molten glass</note>, )
Pound these together. Melt them. As soon as the mixture liquefies, extract it with an iron spoon and put it into a strong lye. In this way it dissolves, and the lye becomes red.

### TO FIX SALTPETRE.

Take 1 lb. of saltpetre in a glazed vessel. Melt it slowly. Sprinkle one ounce of feathery alum (*alumen plumosum*) into the flux. Thus it is fixed and soon becomes an oil. The *alumen plumosum* must previously be pounded small.

### COAGULATION OF MERCURY.

Take arum <note>the plant Cuckoo-pint</note> in May. Pound it with a wooden hammer. Then distill a liquid from it. Pour it over the residue, repeating this up to four times. Pound the dregs continually and let the liquid be consumed. Then make <unclear>seltele die druchne</unclear> (?). Place Mercury in a crucible. When the bubbling begins, throw the powder upon it. Thus the Mercury coagulates into Luna <note>silver</note>.

### OIL OF MERCURY.

Dissolve Mercury in aquafortis <note>nitric acid</note>. Allow it to boil. Remove it from the fire and stir for three hours in an open glass vessel. Then take the Mercury out. Dry it. Grind it upon a stone. Place it in a moist cellar. In this way, it becomes an oil or liquid.

### KING.

Take *alumen de pluma* <note>feather alum</note>. Pour vinegar over it and distill it into a liquid. This liquid clarifies new and immature pearls.

### NOTE. CEMENT.

Make the king <note>regulus</note> out of naphtha and marcasite—that is, antimony made white; the latter becomes black as amber, the other white as Luna <note>silver</note>. Cement Sol <note>gold</note> and Luna <note>silver</note> with it, using pounded glass and salt, for twenty-four hours, etc.

### THE EXTRACTION OF MERCURY.

Take aquafortis, to which you should add common water (lest it be too strong) and sal ammoniac. If you evaporate this water, you will have oil of antimony, with which you can test anything.

### WHEN YOU WISH TO DISSOLVE MERCURY SUBLIMATE AND WHITE MARCASITE (PERHAPS BISMUTH).

Put the sal ammoniac into aquafortis, and they will dissolve; otherwise they will not. Aquafortis is made of vitriol, saltpeter, alum, cinnabar, and verdigris.

->NOTE.<-

Take oil of tartar and oil <note>perhaps "oil of oil" or a specific chemical symbol</note> over an amalgam of Luna <note>silver</note> and Mercury in equal quantities. Mercury will then be fixed, as Hans Rormeyer has stated.

### THE SECRET PHILOSOPHICAL WATER COAGULATING MERCURY AND FIXING LUNA.

Make aquafortis out of vitriol and saltpeter in equal quantities. Take away the first water. Take 1 pound <note>lb.j.</note> of the other. Add 8 <note>viij.</note> parts of verdigris and 8 parts of vitriol beaten small. Seal it up well, and put it in a bath for nine days. Afterwards, distill it through a filter. This water dissolves all bodies and coagulates Mercury. It is the secret of the philosophers. Place the Moon <note>silver</note> upon plates.

### AUGMENT OF THE MOON.

Take 1 marc of Mercury. Form a paste with 1 dram <note>ʒj.</note> of sulphur and one ounce of arsenic. Then pound with them four ounces of iron filings. Make cinnabar with all of it. Take up 1 marc of Luna <note>silver</note> and 3 ounces <note>oz. iij.</note> of cinnabar. Should the Luna have remained in the test, throw it upon it and it augments itself.
