### Note.

Take 1 pound of sugar candy. Put it in a tin can. Pour into it four parts of good white wine. Put all of this in a kettle with water. Close the cans (*sic*) well with the upper lid. Then boil it so that at least one can's worth is well boiled. Then pour another can of wine upon the remaining matter. Do this in the same fashion five times and you will have the oil. Lay the ingredients therein as you wish. Take one ounce of oil or of any kind of aromatic ingredient. Pour a wine into it again, as described above, and let it boil as before. Then you will find a black matter at the bottom of it; extract the oil by means of a filter, and reserve it for use as you know. Lay the ingredients according to your pleasure in the oil. Boil it and you will have an artificial balsam. Take a drop or two of it. Drink it with wine and it colors itself.

## Of the Water which dissolves Sol or Luna.

Take calx of the Sun <note>Gold</note> or Moon <note>Silver</note>. Grind it. Cleanse it with water of salt alkali. Place it in a dissolving vessel, and when it has been dissolved you will have perennial water. This water fixes spirits and solidifies [coagulates] Mercury. (Perhaps alkali of the Philosophers would be better.)

### Note.

Take a common aquafortis <note>nitric acid</note>. Dissolve Luna <note>Silver</note> in it. Place Mercury made into a paste with sulfur, as you know. Extract it eight times, and test it in the cupel <note>cineritium</note>. If you add oil of soap to it, it will then be completed.

### Oil of Soap.

Shave the soap into small pieces. Add crushed [beaten] tile to it. Distill it through a retort. Prick the leaves (*sic*). It fixes all spirits.

### Salpetra Lupi.

Take equal parts of vitriol, saltpeter, and alum. Make aquafortis and dissolve in it as much Mercury as possible. Then extract the water by an alembic, and finally apply a great fire of sublimation, so that the spirits may leave the water. Having cooled the vessel, let what was sublimated and what remained at the bottom be dissolved again in the same water, which should then be extracted once more by an alembic. Do this five times, always giving a fire of sublimation at the end, and at the fifth time it does not ascend. It remains at the bottom as red as blood. Keep this.

Next take 1 pound of sal ammoniac sublimated once by iron filings; and an equal weight of the above-mentioned Mercury. Sublimate five times. Then put it on marble to be dissolved, and let it become a red oil, which you should also preserve.

Take Sol <note>Gold</note> which has been calcined and five times sublimated, with an equal weight of the above-mentioned sal ammoniac. Put this to dissolve; and you will have a red liquid, which you must keep. Then take 1 ounce of oil of Mercury and 1 ounce of liquor of the Sun [liquor solis]. Mix and solidify. Take one part of this medicine, cast [project] it onto twenty-five parts of calcined Luna <note>Silver</note>, and you will have Sol <note>Gold</note> always remaining at twenty-four degrees <note>karats</note>.

### WATER OF MERCURY.

### TO AUGMENT THE TINCTURE.

### WHEN A THING CONTAINS GOLD OR ANYTHING ELSE AND WILL NOT SEPARATE.

### FOR SATURN.

Take <term>Saturn</term> <note>lead</note> in filings dissolved with <term>acetum</term> <note>vinegar</note>. Distill it by the tongue <note>a specific type of distilling spout or vessel</note> and again by the <term>alembic</term>. Possibly the oil of <term>Jove</term> <note>tin</note> could be produced in the same way.

### FLOWERS OF BODIES.

Take the dregs of wine. Place them in a vessel to a thickness of five fingers. Let there be a <term>circulus</term> <note>a circular support or ring</note> in the middle of the vessel, and on the ring place a wooden cross. Put plates on this cross, and let the opening of the vessel be smeared with the <term>lute of wisdom</term> <note>an airtight alchemical sealant</note>. Place it in a hot furnace for seven days. On the eighth day, take it out and set aside the "flower" <note>the sublimated substance or oxidation</note>, washing it with a brush or simply in water. Let the water settle, strain it through a cloth, and dry the flower. Then proceed as before with the plates.

->Take 1 lb of well-calcined alum,<-
->and 2 lbs of saltpeter.<-

Make <term>aquafortis</term> <note>nitric acid</note> and purge it. Take 4 oz of it. In this, dissolve 2 oz of <term>Luna</term> <note>silver</note>. Take another 2 oz of the aforementioned water. Add a little <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note> to it, and in that water dissolve 2 ounces of metallic or crystalline arsenic. Take another two ounces, add sal ammoniac, and dissolve 2 ounces of sublimated <term>Mercury</term> <note>quicksilver</note>. Keep these waters separate, each by itself. Then dissolve 1 lb of purged <term>Venus</term> <note>copper</note> in the said aquafortis; this solution takes, for example, twenty-four <term>lotones</term> <note>a unit of weight, roughly half an ounce</note>. Once these are dissolved, combine all the waters in a large <term>cucurbit</term> <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</note>. Pour a fourth part of water onto it. Let it stand for three hours to mix. Afterward, distill the water from it using an <term>alembic</term> <note>distilling apparatus</note>; the <term>feces</term> <note>solid residue remaining after the process</note> will remain moist at the bottom. Dry these over a slow fire. Then take saltpeter and melted salt. Mix them with the powder in a <term>crucible</term> <note>a heat-resistant melting pot</note>. Place it in a wind furnace. Melt them together. Pour it into a receiver or crucible smeared with honey or suet. Crush and refine it upon the <term>test</term> <note>a cupel or refining vessel used to assay precious metals</note>; you will then have twelve ounces of Luna.

<summary>This page provides recipes for resolving metallic substances into oils, creating a red gold tincture for silver, and a detailed method for augmenting silver by combining it with dissolved copper and mercury.</summary>

### ROYAL CEMENT.

->Take two parts of brick dust.<-
->Take one part of salt.<-
Moisten with vinegar; grade within it.

### PHYSICAL WATER.

Take <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note> which has been sublimated, distilled, and coagulated three times, and then once more let it be dissolved and distilled. Let the process be repeated three times. If it has been dissolved in <term>aqua vitæ</term> <note>distilled spirits or alcohol</note>, distilled, coagulated, and finally dissolved, it dissolves all calcined and burnt bodies, as well as all calcined and sublimated bodies, with a marvelous solution in a crucible over the fire within the space of a single hour; and this is done by the help of God and by His virtue.

->ALSO.<-

Let us compound our philosophic water by the help of God and His virtue. Take 6 drams of <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note>, dissolved and distilled three times, and 6 drams of rectified oil. Mix them together and let six of the aforementioned plates soak by degrees on <term>porphyry</term> <note>a hard rock used for grinding</note> or on a glass table until they have thoroughly absorbed it. When all is absorbed, put it in a glass vessel under horse dung for three days. On the fourth day, pour this onto three pounds of the <term>aqua vitæ</term> <note>distilled alcohol</note> already described, and place it in a <term>venter equinus</term> <note>a "horse's belly," a warm bath of fermenting manure used for gentle heat</note> for fifteen days. On the sixteenth day, you will find the plate dissolved into a white water like milk. Change the dung every fourth day. Complete this water; this is the philosophic oil, a water that penetrates and calms, lighting candles and illuminating the house, and by which all philosophers are sustained. With this, every volatile substance—such as <term>Mercury</term>, <term>Sulphur</term>, and <term>Arsenic</term>—is restrained from escaping.

### THE WHITE.

Take equal quantities of <term>Mercurialis</term> <note>the herb mercury</note> and <term>Saccharum</term> <note>sugar</note>. Mix them and let them stand for nine days. After this, extract the oil according to the fashion of common people. That is perfect, if perfectly produced. If it is placed in a glass globe, it shines at night and creates a beautiful color on the face of a man or a woman. If anyone drinks this oil every morning, even if he is 100 years old, he shall have the complexion of a young man; all his limbs will be light, and he will not be able to be in low spirits. Taking this oil for 40 days on an empty stomach perfectly cures epilepsy of 40 years' standing, as well as asthma. The "White" strengthens a man's nerves beyond all other kinds. Mixed with castor oil and applied to the bone, it removes all contraction of the limbs and cures paralysis of the nerves. For these reasons, we present it as precious. One drop of this "White" put in the eye every morning clears the eyes and keeps them healthy.

->ALSO.<-

Take <unclear>white (? cadmia)</unclear>, gold leaf, oriental pearls, and <term>rhabarbarum</term> <note>rhubarb</note> in equal parts. Grind them together. This is the best medicine for leprosy, which it entirely cures if it is taken each morning on an empty stomach. It produces

### OTHERWISE

Take equal parts of <term>Mercurialis</term> <note>likely the plant Mercury or a mercurial preparation</note> and <term>Meter</term> <note>an obscure term, possibly referring to a measure or a specific mineral substance</note>. Mix them so that the Mercury is previously heated. Then allow it to stand for nine days. Afterward, extract the oil according to the method of the common people. This oil is perfect, etc.

### A LIGHT WHICH ALWAYS BURNS.

Take any quantity of sugar and an equal amount of Mercury. Mix them thoroughly and leave the mixture to stand for 13 or 14 days. Afterward, distill it as an oil. Then take a small linen cloth and press the oil through it. If it were put in a glass, it would shine like a light.

### FIXATION OF MERCURY.

Take alum and dregs of wine. Dissolve them in urine and distill them through a filter. Then dissolve sulfur in it by boiling. Place Mercury in it and let it boil over a gentle fire, continually stirring it, so that it may escape the fire.

**NOTE.**—*Certain formulas and quantities which occur in the* MANUAL OF PARACELSUS *are either unique to the treatise or have long fallen into disuse, and it is difficult to identify their meaning.*
